pair_classification.manual_curation_answer: Yes, the arm is a reviewed domain-prior mechanism. It consumes curated graph-node mappings, subsystem memberships, and manual explicit pairs bound to official references. The algorithm itself is deterministic and does not learn these mappings from feature values.
pair_classification.physical_subsystem_encoding_answer: Yes. Shared reviewed subsystem membership is the M3 fallback evidence tier, after explicit-pair and directed-graph evidence.

ranking.score_interpretation: There is no continuous or weighted META score.

ranking.tie_breaking: canonical source then target lexical order after tier and independent-reference count

top_k.selection: Each view is a prefix of the one supported-pair ranking; top20 is consumed by integration.

pseudocode: Replay the exact frozen C0 config and protocol bundle; require P1 Boiler, 12 sources, 12 targets, 144 ordered eligible pairs, and exact identity hashes.
Verify the ignored reviewed-metadata declaration is self-hashed, uses only approved official references, and covers every frozen source and target binding exactly once.
Verify the official manual and directed P1 physical-graph bytes against their pinned identities; parse and validate the graph node and link structure.

For each canonical source-target pair: choose M1 if manually explicit; else M2 if mapped nodes have an ordered directed graph edge; else M3 if reviewed subsystem memberships overlap; else UNSUPPORTED.
Store one canonical evidence record per pair and assert exact 144-record closure.
Remove UNSUPPORTED records from ranking. Sort supported records by tier, independent reference count descending, source lexical, then target lexical.
Take top10, top20, and top40 prefixes of that single ranking without padding. Record any shortfall.
Build and validate the closed, self-hashed public result. Integration later consumes META top20 and retains META rank/evidence provenance in an unscored cross-arm union.

claim_assessment.META_relation_candidate_meaning: A P1 ordered source-target pair prioritized by reviewed manual, directed physical-graph, or shared-subsystem evidence under a fixed categorical policy.

unknowns_and_limitations.finding: The primary top-20 budget is preregistered and source-supported, but its scientific rationale is not documented in the inspected META implementation or public result.
The public contract proves reviewed mappings and exact reference binding, but it does not independently certify a named human review process or the physical correctness of the mappings.
The official P1 physical graph is deliberately bounded as a weak relation reference, not causal truth; its scientific validity is not established by this discovery execution.
The arm's unique confirmed-relation contribution and stability across alternative metadata policies remain future EXP-01 questions.

coordinator_notes: Describe META as reviewed metadata/domain-prior candidate ranking, not as a learned or causal relation method.
The word score should be qualified: META has a categorical lexicographic ranking key, not a numerical score.
Direction here is ordered source-to-target candidate identity supported by directed graph/manual semantics; final delayed-response direction and horizon belong to downstream relation profiling.
The 30 supported-pair count explains why top40 returns only 30; no unsupported pair is added to meet a budget.
The top20 is a policy choice frozen before downstream evaluation, but the inspected evidence does not state a scientific rationale for choosing 20.
